# creating Functions
```{r}
testfun <- function(){
  print("this function does nothing")
}
testfun()
#functions with inputs in the () and give outputs in the {} (usually)
testfun <- function(sometext){
  print(sometext)
}
testfun("this function does slightly more, but still not much")
#function that calculate something
#just write fun --> u get the basic structure
my_age <- function(birthday) {
  today <- Sys.Date()
  as.numeric(difftime(today, birthday, units = "days")/365.25)
}

my_age("2001-07-09")

#function more flexible
testfun("this function does slightly more, but still not much")
#function that calculate something
#just write fun --> u get the basic structure
#if nothing specified --> output unit = auto
my_age <- function(birthday, output_unit = "auto") {
  today <- Sys.Date()
  difftime(today, birthday, units = output_unit)
}

my_age(birthday= "2001-07-09", output_unit= "secs")
my_age("2001-07-09")
#if you have a problem with the function, write browser() into the function --> u can debug the function --> then stop and remove the browser --> reexcecute the function (also possible to use within loops)

bmi <- function(weight, height){
  bmi_value <- weight/height^2
  bmi_value
}
bmi(80, 1.60)
#the last line is return (automatically)
bmi <- function(weight, height){
  bmi_value <- weight/height^2
  return(bmi_value)
}
bmi(80, 1.60)
#new way 
bim2 <- \(weight,height)weight/height ^2
```
